description: Complete beat type definitions for ASAPS Modern with nested connection architecture and cluster container support

connectionModel.description: Defines how connections are structured within beats
principles: Connections are semantically part of the function's behavior
Single-connection beats have connection within function
Multi-connection beats have choices/props that contain targets
All connections support labels, conditions, and effects

dialogNode.description: A node in a dialog tree representing NPC/system output. Always followed by player choices.
dialogNode.notes: dialogNode displays text and waits for player to click a choice. No auto-advance.

dialogChoice.description: A player choice in dialog. Can exit to a beat or continue with nested dialog.
dialogChoice.notes: Either 'target' (beat ID to exit) OR 'dialogNode' (continue conversation), not both. Counter fields allow direct counter modification (any counter name) in addition to effects[]. soundEffect plays when this choice is selected.

movementOption.notes: Counter fields allow direct counter modification (any counter name) in addition to effects[]. soundEffect plays when this choice is selected. locationName optionally references a hotspot or prop from beat.locations by name. displayText is the translated/display label; text is the internal identifier used for hotspot matching.

propOption.notes: If assetId is provided, prop is rendered as clickable graphic from assets. Otherwise rendered as button. Counter fields allow direct counter modification. soundEffect plays when this prop is selected. locationName optionally references a hotspot or prop from beat.locations by name for Visual Editor association. inventoryName overrides the item name added to inventory (defaults to locationName or name). displayName overrides the label shown on hotspots (defaults to name). Useful for translations where name must stay as internal key.

aiNotes.structure: dialogTree alternates: dialogNode (NPC speaks) → choices (player clicks - text IS player's dialogue) → dialogNode (NPC responds) → choices...
aiNotes.pattern: Each dialogNode has speaker, text, and choices array. Player must click a choice to continue.
aiNotes.choiceNavigation: Each choice has text (player's line) and EITHER 'target' (beat ID to exit) OR 'dialogNode' (NPC responds), never both
aiNotes.critical: Choice text IS the player's dialogue. NEVER use '[Continue]' or placeholder text. Every choice should be meaningful player dialogue.
aiNotes.effects: Use effects on choices to modify counters or variables when player selects that choice
aiNotes.example: { id: 'root', speaker: 'NPC', text: 'Hello!', choices: [{ id: 'c1', text: 'Hi there!', dialogNode: { id: 'n1', speaker: 'NPC', text: 'Nice day!', choices: [{ id: 'c2', text: 'Indeed it is. Goodbye!', target: 'next_beat' }] } }] }
